0x8205F64C: Bring the outfield in to stop the runner on second from scoring on a single.
0x8205F688: Look for a double play through second or a force at home.
0x8205F6B8: Prioritize the force at home to keep the runner on third from scoring.
0x8205F6F8: The corner infielders charge as the pitch begins, looking for the force at second.
0x8205F73C: Take the sure out against a sacrifice bunt.
0x8205F76C: Set up a double play through second base.
0x8205F790: Take the out on the batter-runner at first.
0x8205FB28:
Each pitch has its own Control rating.
Low Control makes Direct Pitching's release
timing harder to judge. A Best Pitch still
improves accuracy, even with low Control.
0x8205FBE8:
Each pitch has its own Stuff rating.
Higher Stuff makes breaking pitches break
later, closer to the batter. It also makes
the Pitch Marker smaller and helps fastballs
retain more of their speed.
0x8205FCC8:
Recovery determines how quickly players
recover from fatigue in Pennant mode.
A high rating helps a player perform
consistently throughout a full season.
0x8205FD78:
A position's Fielding rating affects the
fielder's first step and acceleration.
For infielders, a strong Fielding rating can
be more important than raw Speed.
0x8205FE38:
Catching affects how reliably and quickly
a fielder gets into position to field a ball.
For catchers, it also helps prevent passed
balls and stop pitches in the dirt.
0x8205FEC0:
Throwing affects the accuracy and speed of
a fielder's throws. A high rating reduces
throwing errors and helps the fielder make
reliable throws from awkward positions.
0x8205FF60:
Trajectory affects the launch angle of balls
hit with a Power Swing. Higher ratings make
home-run trajectories more likely, but also
produce more pop-ups. There are seven levels.
0x82060028:
Contact has separate ratings against
right-handed and left-handed pitchers.
Try different lineups to make the most of
each batter's strengths.
0x820600A8:
Pitch type, handedness, delivery, and location
all affect how the ball looks to the batter.
Hitting your spot improves Stuff; missing
it reduces Stuff. Experiment to develop
your own pitching style.
0x82060198:
Repeated pitches to the same location can
turn a batter's cold zone into a hot zone.
The opposite side becomes harder to see
and gradually turns cold. Vary your locations.
0x82060258:
Colors in the strike zone show the batter's
hot and cold zones. Red is a hot zone;
blue is a cold zone. Attack the batter's
weak spots to keep them off balance.
0x82060318:
Press to bunt. Use a normal bunt when
you need to advance a runner reliably.
Hold for a push bunt, which can also
help when trying to bunt for a hit.
0x820603C8:
Before batting, press to switch between
Power and Contact Swings. Power Swings hit
the ball harder, but shrink the contact zone
and leave a smaller timing window.
0x82060490:
An ordinary walk can shake a pitcher and
increase fatigue. Calling an intentional
walk through the team signs avoids those
penalties.
0x82060530:
With Defensive Formation set to Pro,
fielders cover only the bases needed for
the play. The others back up throws or
help with rundowns.
0x820605F0:
With the ball, press to throw to the
cutoff man. You can also use this during
a rundown. It has no effect if no cutoff
man is available.
0x820606B8:
Hold the throw button before the ball is
caught for a quicker, smoother release.
Choose the base early and keep its button
held while fielding the ball.
0x82060770:
The selected fielder can change automatically
during a play. Hold to keep control of
the current fielder. Try this when tracking
a high fly ball.
0x82060838:
Pitch Speed greatly changes batting
difficulty. If hitting feels too easy,
raise it for a tougher challenge.
0x820608E0:
Set Strike Zone Display to Hot/Cold Only
or Off to make judging balls and strikes
harder. Try this once you are comfortable
with batting.
0x82060990:
With Zone Hitting, timing your swing is
enough to cover the strike zone. Lay off
balls outside the zone. Try combining this
with Real Speed.
0x82060A70:
With Lock-On, the batting cursor tracks the
Pitch Marker automatically during your swing.
Try this if aiming the cursor is difficult.
0x82060B20:
Area Hitting uses a blurred target area
instead of a precise cursor. Try it with
Real Speed or with the Pitch Marker off
for a different batting experience.
0x82060BF0:
Set Catcher Return Throw to Skip to skip
return-throw animations automatically.
Use this to keep games moving.
0x82060C90:
Set Pitching Delivery to Quick to always
use a quick delivery. Try this setting
to keep games moving.
0x82060D28:
Turning the Pitch Marker off hides the ball's
target cursor. Batting becomes tougher,
but combining this with Zone or Area Hitting
creates a different batting experience.
0x82060DF8:
The Real Pitch Marker reflects the actual
path of the pitch. Try it to see how different
breaking pitches and deliveries affect
the ball's movement.
0x82060EA8:
The Easy Pitch Marker also shows where the
pitch will finish after breaking. Try it
if breaking pitches are difficult to hit.
0x82060F70:
The Pitch Marker represents the incoming
ball within the strike zone. Its movement
depends on pitch type, and its size changes
with Stuff, affecting how hard it is to hit.
0x82061048:
If batting is difficult, turn on CPU Pitch
Cursor. It shows where the CPU is aiming,
making pitches easier to track.
0x820610D0:
A visible pitching cursor reveals your target
when playing a friend. Use Fixed Display
to hide the target while keeping the
release-timing indicator visible.
0x82061188:
You can swing with either <×> or <○>.
Use <○> for an opposite-field swing.
This lets you wait longer and hit firmly,
but prevents pulling the ball. Useful when
you want to make reliable contact.
0x820613C8:
You control when a runner advances or
returns, including starts on batted balls
and returns on pickoff attempts. Hold
left to return automatically
on a pickoff, at the cost of a slower start.
0x820614B8:
As an outfielder, handle batted balls and
back up your teammates. On a fly ball,
quickly press to point the camera toward
the landing spot and help line up the catch.
0x82061580:
Infielders must field batted balls and
cover bases. Keep track of the outs and
runners so you can react without hesitation,
especially at second base and shortstop.
0x82061658:
As catcher, call the pitch type and location.
The pitcher controls the release. You also
set defensive shifts, so choose an alignment
that suits the situation.
0x820616E8:
As pitcher, control location and release
timing. The catcher calls the pitch type,
but the left trigger may persuade them
to change it. Remember to cover first base!
0x82061260:
The pitching cursor shows your target and
release timing. Release when it shrinks to
its smallest point for a Best Pitch,
which gives Stuff a large boost.
0x82061308:
Press <×> twice to pitch.
First press: start the delivery.
Second press: release the ball.
Good release timing produces better Stuff.
0x820617A0:
You can develop a created player's
Awakening stats. Buy Awakening Challenge
in the VP Shop before finishing development
to unlock its final stage. Afterwards,
use the VP Shop to awaken the player.
0x82061870:
Development points earned in a game depend
on your player's individual performance.
Drawing a walk earns a positive evaluation,
too.
0x820618E8:
You can develop a created player's
Awakening stats. Buy Awakening Challenge
in the VP Shop before finishing development
to unlock its final stage. Afterwards,
use the VP Shop to awaken the player.
0x820619B8:
In VP Challenge, each home run earns a red
Extra Ball. Hit more home runs with these
balls to build a higher score.
Aim for 20 home runs!
0x82061A68:
The rules are simple: hit as many home runs
into the stands as you can with 10 balls.
Choose VP Challenge to earn VP!
0x82061AF0:
Clear a board to earn a bonus. In VP
Challenge, knocking out two panels at once
earns a red Extra Ball. Use it for another
two-panel hit to score even more points.
0x82061BA0:
Aim at a nine-panel strike board.
Knock out the eight outer panels to clear
the board. Avoid the skull in the center!
0x82061C48:
Set player usage rules under Management
on the Daily Menu. These rules matter most
when you are not watching the game.
Experiment to keep your team running well.
0x82061D08:
Manager Pennant offers three ways to play:
Results: finish games as quickly as possible.
Live Results: follow updates as games run.
Watch Game: watch and make substitutions
yourself.
0x82061DC8:
Take control of one player in Field Play.
Change its progression settings to play
only your at-bats, or only your pitching
appearances if you are a pitcher.
0x82061E88:
Pitchers can use Starter Prep or Relief
Prep. Each gradually improves their rating
in the corresponding role. Choose the
preparation that suits your player's goals.
0x82061F50:
Resting a pitcher in Pennant mode greatly
reduces fatigue. Bringing them into a game
while resting means they are unprepared
and will build up fatigue, so be careful.
0x82062020:
A pitcher on Relief Prep can enter a game
at any time. If they do not pitch that day,
they recover from fatigue as if resting.
0x820620C8:
Starter Prep builds a pitcher's Starter
Stamina each day. Bringing them into relief
unexpectedly during preparation prevents
them from performing at their best.
0x82062180:
Players can build up stress depending on
how they are used. Stress can cause problems,
so pay attention to the coach's comments
on the Player Information screen.
0x82062238:
This mission continues through a set number
of stages unless you fail. Clear every stage
to earn a large MCP reward.
0x820622C8:
Try playing a friend in a Player Match.
Use Invite Friend in the lobby menu
to send an invitation.
0x82062350:
The pitching player must pitch within six
seconds. Once time runs out, the pitch
starts automatically!
0x820623A8:
Co-op pitching takes teamwork:
1. The catcher chooses the pitch type.
2. The pitcher starts the delivery.
3. The catcher chooses the location.
4. The pitcher releases the ball!
0x82062460:
P1 starts as pitcher and P2 as catcher.
Those roles swap after a pitching change.
Players alternate at-bats; a pinch hitter
also switches the batting player.
0x82062508:
Two players team up against the CPU.
One calls pitch type and location as catcher;
the other controls delivery and release.
Take turns batting. The other player
controls any runners on base.
0x82062608:
Control one player in Field Play! Choose
a starter, reliever, catcher, second baseman,
outfielder, or another position.
Practice each position's role in Trial mode.
0x820626D0:
Use team signs to coordinate batters and
runners. For example, call a hit-and-run
with a runner on first: the runner starts
automatically, so you can focus on batting.
0x820627C0:
Keep holding the pitch-start button as the
delivery begins. The cursor grows and turns
red, charging a Power Pitch. It adds Stuff
at the cost of Stamina and accuracy.

You can start a steal before the pitch!
Read the pitcher's timing for a good jump.
Go too early and you risk being picked off.

Manage a team through a Pennant season!
Give instructions without controlling the
players directly. Choose from three ways
to follow the action.
0x820629D8:
Play a Pennant season as one player!
Earn VP with strong performances.
0x82062A40:
Take control of one player and complete
challenges at different positions.
A great way to practice Field Play!
0x82062AC0:
Knock out the nine panels on a strike board
with your pitches. Simple rules, plenty of
challenge! Play as your favorite pitcher.

Features 600 players: 50 on each team!
Every player has individually detailed
